newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures slide as dlr weakens.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures slide as dlr weakens.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed lower across the board on Monday, reflecting the dollar's renewed decline against the yen, traders said.
"There was no news except for the dollar's fall," said one trader. "The key is whether the metal can regain the $1,600 level in London. The dollar is unlikely to fall much further from here."
The TOCOM benchmark April 1998 contract shed 4.4 yen to finish at 188.1 yen per kg, its contract low, while others lost between 4.2 and 5.0 yen.
Estimated trade volume was 2,923 lots, up from a record low of 822 lots on Friday.

The dollar tumbled to 111.80 yen during Asian trade on Monday on the narrowing of the interest rate gap between the United States and Japan, and fears of renewed trade friction between the two countries.
In London on Friday, three-month aluminium ended down $3 at $1,597 after featureless trade.
